newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria gas company urges higher natgas prices.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria gas company urges higher natgas prices.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-owned gas company Bulgargas said on Friday it was losing millions of dollars from selling natural gas at unrealistically low prices on the domestic market, hampering its payments to suppliers.

"Bulgargas is selling natural gas on the domestic market at half the import price and at the end of January the company was forced to sell it at some $63 (per cubic metre) cheaper than its import price," a Bulgargas statement said.

It said the company had suffered a loss of $22 million for the first two months of the year due to low prices and another $8 million due to the drastic fall of the lev to the dollar during this period.
The company urged that domestic sale prices be pegged to the dollar rate.
Bulgargas said it had started curbing natural gas deliveries to its debtors on Thursday.
It cut gas supplies to the country's biggest oil refinery Neftochim earlier this month but restored them after being assured that the plant would find a formula for paying its debts.
"By the end of March Bulgargas had to ensure some $60 million only for natural gas supplies. But how, when less than half of the consumers have paid their debts?
How, when even those who have paid for consumed gas have paid at a price favourable for them which is an absurdity for the new conditions?" the statement said.
Bulgaria, which lacks energy resources, imports all its gas supplies from Russia.
